content.title: What are Threads & Runnable Interface?
content.description: A thread is the smallest unit of execution within a process. Java supports multithreading through the Thread class and the Runnable interface, allowing multiple tasks to execute concurrently.

content.content: Modern applications often need to perform multiple tasks simultaneously, such as downloading files while updating the user interface. Java provides multithreading using the Thread class and the Runnable interface. Threads improve responsiveness and make efficient use of CPU resources.

content.title: Why Learn Threads?
content.content: Threads are essential for building responsive applications, parallel processing, web servers, games, and real-time systems.
A thread is an independent path of execution within a program. Multiple threads can run concurrently, allowing different tasks to execute simultaneously.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Every Java application starts with a single thread called the main thread.

content.content: Creating a Thread using Thread Class
One way to create a thread is by extending the Thread class and overriding its run() method.

content.title: Thread Class Example
Important Note
content.content: Always call start() instead of run(). The start() method creates a new thread, whereas run() executes like a normal method.
The recommended approach is to implement the Runnable interface because it allows a class to extend another class while still supporting multithreading.

content.title: Runnable Example

rows: Waits for another thread to finish

items.question: Improved Performance
items.answer: Multiple tasks can execute simultaneously on multi-core processors.

items.question: Responsive Applications
items.answer: Long-running tasks do not freeze the user interface.

items.question: Efficient CPU Utilization
items.answer: CPU resources are better utilized by running multiple threads.

items.question: Parallel Processing
items.answer: Large computations can be divided among multiple threads.

items.question: Games
items.answer: Separate rendering, input handling, and physics calculations.

items.question: Background Tasks
items.answer: Perform logging, backups, and scheduled operations.

content.title: Restaurant Kitchen
content.content: Imagine several chefs working in the same kitchen. One prepares appetizers, another cooks the main course, while another makes desserts. Each chef represents a thread performing a different task simultaneously.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Thread creation, Runnable vs Thread, lifecycle, start() vs run(), join(), sleep(), synchronization, daemon threads, and thread safety are frequently asked Java interview topics.

items.question: Should run() be called directly?
items.answer: No. Calling run() executes the method in the current thread. Use start() to create a new thread.

items.question: Is extending Thread always recommended?
items.answer: No. Implementing Runnable is generally preferred because it allows inheritance from another class.

items.question: Can multiple threads safely modify shared data?
items.answer: Not always. Synchronization or concurrent collections are required to prevent race conditions.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Use Runnable for better flexibility and always start threads using the start() method instead of calling run() directly.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: A thread is an independent execution path.
Every Java program starts with the main thread.
Threads can be created using Thread or Runnable.
Always use start() to begin thread execution.
Thread lifecycle includes New, Runnable, Running, Waiting, and Terminated states.
